concepts.name: Firm's financial objective
concepts.summary: Explain that corporate finance decisions aim to maximise firm value for owners, and distinguish this from maximising accounting profit.

concepts.name: Three core financial decisions
concepts.summary: Recall the investment, financing and payout decisions and what each asks a manager to decide.

concepts.name: Time value of money
concepts.summary: Explain why a dollar today is worth more than a dollar later because of earning capacity and risk.

concepts.name: Present and future value
concepts.summary: Describe how compounding moves a sum forward and discounting brings it back to today at a given rate.

concepts.name: Risk and required return
concepts.summary: Explain that riskier cash flows demand higher expected returns from investors.

concepts.name: Debt versus equity
concepts.summary: Recall that debt is a contractual borrowing with interest while equity is ownership with residual claims.

concepts.name: Cash flow versus profit
concepts.summary: Explain why finance values cash flows rather than accounting earnings.

misconceptions.text: A company's goal is to maximise its accounting profit each year.
Money's value over time changes only because of inflation.
Debt is always cheaper and therefore always better than equity.

concepts.name: Annuities and perpetuities
concepts.summary: Compute present and future values of level and growing payment streams using standard formulas.

concepts.name: Incremental project cash flows
concepts.summary: Build project cash flows from only incremental items, including working capital, capex and after-tax operating flows, and ignore sunk costs.

concepts.name: Net present value calculation
concepts.summary: Discount a project's forecast cash flows at the required return and accept it when the NPV is positive.

concepts.name: Internal rate of return
concepts.summary: Find the discount rate that sets NPV to zero and compare it to the required return.

concepts.name: Payback and simple rules
concepts.summary: Calculate payback periods and explain why they ignore value beyond the cutoff or the time value.

concepts.name: Cost of debt and equity
concepts.summary: Compute the after-tax cost of debt and a basic cost of equity from observed yields or dividends.

concepts.name: Working capital cycle
concepts.summary: Calculate days inventory, receivables and payables and combine them into the cash conversion cycle.

misconceptions.text: Sunk costs and allocated overhead should be included in a project's cash flows.
A project with a short payback period is always a good investment.
IRR is the return the firm will actually earn on reinvested cash flows.

concepts.name: NPV versus IRR conflicts
concepts.summary: Diagnose when IRR and NPV disagree because of scale, timing or non-conventional cash flows and resolve it in favour of NPV.

concepts.name: Capital rationing and comparison
concepts.summary: Rank projects under a budget constraint or unequal lives using profitability index and equivalent annual annuity.

concepts.name: CAPM and beta
concepts.summary: Estimate cost of equity from the risk-free rate, equity beta and market risk premium and explain systematic risk.

concepts.name: Weighted average cost of capital
concepts.summary: Compute WACC using market-value weights and after-tax debt cost, and use it as the discount rate for average-risk projects.

concepts.name: Sensitivity and scenario analysis
concepts.summary: Test how NPV changes with key assumptions to identify the drivers of project risk.

concepts.name: Tax shield and leverage
concepts.summary: Analyse why capital structure is irrelevant without frictions and how interest tax shields change value.

concepts.name: Working capital financing policy
concepts.summary: Compare aggressive and conservative funding of current assets and the trade-off of cost, liquidity and risk.

concepts.name: Dividend and repurchase choices
concepts.summary: Describe how dividends and buybacks distribute cash and evaluate their effect on shareholders' wealth.

misconceptions.text: The project with the highest IRR is always the one that adds the most value.
A firm's WACC is the correct discount rate for every project it undertakes.
Equity is free or cheaper than debt because dividends are optional.

concepts.name: Project-specific discount rates
concepts.summary: Unlever and relever comparable-firm betas to set discount rates that match each project's business risk.

concepts.name: Adjusted present value
concepts.summary: Value a project by adding financing side effects to its all-equity NPV when capital structure changes.

concepts.name: Real options in investment
concepts.summary: Judge how options to delay, expand or abandon add value that static NPV misses.

concepts.name: Simulation and risk-adjusted valuation
concepts.summary: Assess project risk using probabilistic simulation and decide how to treat it in rates versus cash flows.

concepts.name: Agency problems in finance
concepts.summary: Analyse how conflicts among managers, shareholders and creditors distort investment and financing choices.

concepts.name: Trade-off and pecking order
concepts.summary: Evaluate a firm's leverage using tax benefits, distress costs, agency costs and information asymmetry.

concepts.name: Capital issuance and signalling
concepts.summary: Interpret issuance costs and market reactions to debt, equity and payout announcements.

concepts.name: Optimal cash management
concepts.summary: Evaluate credit terms, inventory and cash holdings by weighing carrying costs against shortage costs.

misconceptions.text: Using the firm's WACC is fine even when a project's risk differs sharply from the firm's.
Static NPV already captures the value of managerial flexibility.
Raising leverage always lowers WACC and so always raises firm value.

concepts.name: Designing capital allocation frameworks
concepts.summary: Create a firm-wide process for generating, screening, approving and auditing investments that limits bias and gaming.

concepts.name: Critiquing valuation assumptions
aliases: terminal value and discount rate scrutiny
concepts.summary: Evaluate forecasts, terminal values and discount rates in a valuation to expose where most value is concentrated.

concepts.name: Optimal capital structure design
concepts.summary: Construct a financing policy that sets target leverage, debt maturity and covenants for a specific firm's risks and growth options.

concepts.name: Financial flexibility and risk management
concepts.summary: Judge when hedging and liquidity reserves protect investment capacity and when they destroy value.

concepts.name: Corporate restructuring and M&A valuation
concepts.summary: Appraise acquisitions, spin-offs and leveraged buyouts by separating synergies, control premia and financing effects.

concepts.name: Payout policy under uncertainty
concepts.summary: Design payout policy that balances investment needs, signalling, taxes and investor clienteles.

concepts.name: International corporate finance
concepts.summary: Evaluate foreign projects by handling exchange rates, country risk and differing tax regimes consistently in cash flows and discount rates.

misconceptions.text: A sophisticated valuation model gives a precise answer, so the judgement behind inputs matters little.
Hedging always creates value for shareholders because it reduces volatility.
Acquisitions create value whenever the target is profitable or earnings per share rises.
